children.translated_text: <s>Mattavilāsaprahasana</s> (The Farce of Drunken Sport), composed by the illustrious <s>Mahendravikramavarman</s>.
(After the benedictory verse, the <s>Sūtradhāra</s> (stage manager) enters.)

children.text:
bhāṣāveṣavapuḥkriyāguṇakṛtān āśritya bhedān gataṃ
bhāvāveśavaśād anekarasatāṃ trailokyayātrāmayam /
nṛttaṃ niṣpratibaddhabodhamahimā yaḥ (1) prekṣakaś ca svayaṃ
sa vyāptāvanibhājanaṃ diśatu vo divyaḥ kapālī yaśaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: May He, the divine <s>Kapālī</s> (skull-bearer, i.e. <s>Śiva</s>), who through the distinctions created by language, costume, body, action, and qualities has attained manifold <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavors) by the force of emotional possession — whose dance constitutes the spectacle of the three worlds, who is Himself the spectator of unobstructed wisdom's glory — may He, who pervades the vessel of the earth, bestow upon you glory! ||1||

children.text:
bhoḥ ! samāsāditaḥ khalu mayā yavīyasīṃ bhāryāṃ adhikṛtya samutpannavyalīkāyāṃ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ me kuṭumbinyāṃ yuktataraḥ prasādanopāyaḥ, yac cirasyādya vayaṃ prekṣādhikāre pariṣadā niyuktāḥ smaḥ / tad yāvad enām upasarpāmi / ({parikramya CDEH} nepathyābhimukham avalokya) ārye ! itas tāvat /
(praviśya)
children.translated_text: Well! I have indeed found a most fitting means of appeasing my senior wife, who has become resentful on account of the younger wife — for after a long time, today we have been appointed by the assembly to oversee the performance. So let me approach her. (Walking around, looking toward the backstage) Lady! Come here, please! (She enters.)

children.text:
- (saroṣam) ayya! kiṃ cirassa kālassa jovvaṇa{guṇa : guṇṇa H}bharamattavilāsappahasaṇaṃ (o?daṃ)seduṃ (2) āado si /
[ārya! kiṃ cirasya kālasya yauvanaguṇabharamattavilāsaprahasanaṃ darśayitum āgato 'si /]
children.translated_text: (Angrily) My lord! After such a long time, have you come to show me the <s>Mattavilāsaprahasana</s> (Farce of Drunken Sport) — intoxicated with the burden of youth's charms?

children.text:
- tāe eva {dāva : dāṇiṃ D} daṃsehi, jā tue ramaidavvā /
[tayaiva tāvad darśaya, yā tvayā ramayitavyā /]
children.translated_text: — Then first show me her — the one you are to sport with!
— I shall perform it together with you!

children.text:
- kiṃ tāe evva ṇiutto si /
[kiṃ tayaiva niyukto 'si /]
children.translated_text: — Have you been appointed by her alone?

children.text: - evam etat / api ca, tatra gatā mahāntam anugrahaṃ lapsyase /
children.translated_text: — Indeed so. Moreover, by going there you will receive great favor.

children.text:
- tava evva khu edaṃ jujjai /
[{tavaiva : tathaivaṃ G} khalv etad yujyate /]
- bhavati! kim iva na yujyate / tvatprayogaparitoṣitā pariṣad anurahīṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: — My lady! How does it not befit? The audience, delighted by your performance, will be well-disposed!

children.text:
- (saharṣam) evaṃ / laddho ayyamissāṇaṃ pasādo /
[evam / labdha āryamiśrāṇāṃ prasādaḥ /]
children.translated_text: (With delight) Indeed! I have received the favor of the noble masters!

children.text:
- jai evaṃ, kiṃ de piakkhāṇiaṃ demi /
[yady evaṃ, kiṃ te {priyākhyānikaṃ : priyākhyānitakaṃ G} dadāmi /]
children.translated_text: — If so, shall I give you a love-token?
— Enough with the redundancy of love-tokens! Look —

children.text:
udbhinnaromāñcakapolarekham
āvirmayūkhasmitam añcitabhru /
labdhvā priye durlabham ānanaṃ te
bhūyo 'pi kiṃ prārthayitavyam asti // 2 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained, O beloved, your rarely-won face — with cheek-lines of bristling goosebumps, a smile revealed like radiant beams, and arched brows — what more need be desired? ||2||

children.text:
- kiṃ dāṇi ayyeṇa paujjidavvaṃ /
[kim idānīm āryeṇa {prayoktavyam : nāṭakaṃ nāṭayitavyam G} /]
children.translated_text: — What is to be performed now by the master?
— Why, you yourself have named it — the <s>Mattavilāsaprahasana</s> (Farce of Drunken Sport)!

children.text:
- ṇūṇaṃ {imassiṃ : imasmi Unni} pakkhavādī me kovo, jeṇa abhippāāṇu{rūvaṃ : gadaṃ Kha} bhaṇāvida hmi / ayya! kadamo uṇa so kavī, jo imāe kidīe paāsīadi /
[{nūnam : ām G} asmin pakṣapātī me kopaḥ, yenābhiprāyānurūpaṃ bhāṇitāsmi / ārya! katamaḥ punaḥ sa kaviḥ, {yo 'nayā kṛtyā prakāsyate : yenānayā kṛtyā ātmānam eva prakāśayiṣyati G} /]
children.translated_text: — Surely my anger takes my side, for I have been made to speak according to my own wish! My lord, who then is that poet who will become famous through this work?

children.text: - bhavati! śrūyatām / {vidita D}pallavakuladharaṇimaṇḍala{kula : om. H}parvatasya sarvanayavijitasamastasāmantamaṇḍalasya ākhaṇḍalasamaparākramaśriyaḥ śrimahimānurūpadānavibhūtiparibhūtarājarājasya śrīsiṃhaviṣṇuvarmaṇaḥ putraḥ śatruṣaḍvarganigrahaparaḥ parahitaparatantratayā mahābhūtasadharmā mahārājaḥ śrīmahendravikramavarmā nāma / api ca -
children.translated_text: — My lady, listen! The son of the illustrious <s>Siṃhaviṣṇuvarman</s> — crown of the <s>Pallava</s> dynasty that is the mountain supporting the circle of the earth, who has conquered the entire circle of feudatories through every stratagem, whose glory of valor equals that of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who humbles the king of kings through generous wealth befitting his great majesty — the great king named the illustrious <s>Mahendravikramavarman</s>, devoted to subduing the six inner enemies, who, being devoted to the welfare of others, shares the nature of the great elements. Moreover —

children.text:
prajñādānadayānubhāvadhṛtayaḥ kāntiḥ kalākauśalaṃ
satyaṃ śauryam amāyatā vinaya ityevamprakārā guṇāḥ /
aprāptasthitayaḥsametyaśaraṇaṃ yātā yam ekaṃ kalau
kalpānte jagadādim ādipuruṣaṃ sargaprabhedā iva // 3 //
children.translated_text: Wisdom, generosity, compassion, dignity, steadfastness, beauty, skill in the arts, truthfulness, valor, guilelessness, and humility — qualities of such a kind, having found no abode and seeking refuge, have gone to him alone in the <s>Kali</s> age, like the varieties of creation returning to the primordial Being at the end of the cosmic cycle. ||3||
In him, who is a mine of gem-like good sayings weighted with virtues,

children.text: arghanti (3) bahu sūktāni satāṃ sāralaghūny api // 4 //
children.translated_text: even the simple and concise good sayings of the virtuous are valued highly. ||4||

children.text:
- kiṃ dāṇi ayyeṇa vilambīadi / ṇaṃ apuruvadāe turiaṃ aṇuṭṭhidavvo aaṃ paoo /
[kim idānīm āryeṇa vilambyate / nanv apūrvatayā tvaritam anuṣṭhātavyo 'yaṃ prayogaḥ /]
children.translated_text: — Why does the master delay now? This performance should be undertaken swiftly, given its novelty!
Now, though my wealth lies in music, I have been brought to naught by narrating the poet's virtues. ||5ab||
Here comes one whose companion is a young woman and whose wealth is the wine-cup — like a <s>Kapālī</s> whose glory lies in the skull! ||5cd||
(Then enters the <s>Kapālī</s> (skull-bearing ascetic) with his consort.)

children.text: - (kṣībatāṃ rūpayitvā) priye! devasome! satyam evaitat - tapasā kāmarūpatā prāpyata iti / yat tvayā paramavratasya vidhivadanuṣṭhānenānya eva rūpātiśayaḥ kṣaṇāt pratipannaḥ / tava hi -
children.translated_text: (Affecting drunkenness) Beloved! <s>Devasomā</s>! It is truly so — through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), the power to assume any form is attained! For through your proper performance of the supreme vow, a surpassing beauty of form has been instantly acquired. For you —

children.text:
udbhinnaśramavāribinu vadanaṃ sabhrūlatāvibhramaṃ
khelaṃ yātam akāraṇāni hasitāny avyaktavarṇā giraḥ /
rāgākrāntam adhīratāramalasāpāṅgaṃ yugaṃ netrayor
aṃsopāntavilambinaś ca vigalanmālāguṇā mūrdhajāḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: Your face beaded with drops of exertion's moisture, playful with the graceful movement of your brow-creepers; your gait has become sportive; your laughter is causeless; your words of indistinct syllables; your pair of eyes, overcome with passion, with unsteady pupils and languid side-glances; and your hair, with garland-strings loosening, hanging to the edges of your shoulders. ||6||

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! mattaṃ via mattaṃ via maṃ bhanāsi /
[bhagavan! mattām iva mattām iva māṃ bhaṇasi /]
children.translated_text: — My lord! You describe me as if I were drunk, as if drunk!

children.text:
- ṇa hu kiñci bhaṇāmi /
[na khalu kiñcid bhaṇāmi /]
- bhaavaṃ! paribbhamai paribbhamai puhuvī / puro vadāmi via / avalamba dāṇi maṃ / [bhagavan! paribhramati paribhramati pṛthivī / puraḥ patāmīva / valambasvedānīṃ mām /]
children.translated_text: — My lord! The earth is spinning, spinning! I am about to fall forward! Support me now!

children.text: - priye! {tathāstu : tathā D} / (avalambamānaḥ patanaṃ rūpayitvā) priye! somadeve! kiṃ tvaṃ kupitāsi, yad avalambitum upasarpato me dūrībhavasi /
children.translated_text: — Beloved! So be it! (Supporting her, feigning a fall) Beloved! <s>Somadevā</s>! Are you angry, that you move away from me as I approach to support you?

children.text:
- aho ṇu khu āadakovā somadevā, jā tue sīseṇa paṇamia aṇuṇīamāṇā vi durīhoi /
[aho nu khalv āgatakopā somadevā, yā tvayā śīrṣeṇa praṇamyānunīyamānāpi dūrībhavati /]
children.translated_text: — Oh, <s>Somadevā</s> is truly angry indeed, she who moves away even when you bow your head and try to appease her!

children.text: - nanu tvam evāsi somadevā / (dhyātvā) na hi {na hi D}, devasomā /
children.translated_text: — But you yourself are <s>Somadevā</s>! (Reflecting) No, no — <s>Devasomā</s>!

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! ṇaṃ tahā vallahā somadevā, ṇārhadi mama ṇāmakeṇābhidhāduṃ /
[bhagavan! nanu tathā vallabhā somadevā, nārhati mama {nāmakenābhidhātum : nāmadheyenābhidhātum G} /]
children.translated_text: — My lord! If <s>Somadevā</s> is so dear to you, you should not address her by my name!

children.text: - bhavati! sulabhapadaskhalito me mado 'yaṃ {tavātrāparāddhaḥ : tavātrāparādhyati EG} /
children.translated_text: — My lady! This intoxication of mine, which so easily stumbles in its words, has offended you herein.
— Fortunately, it is not you [but the intoxication]!

children.text: - kathaṃ madyadoṣo mām evaṃ saṅkrāmayati / bhavatu {bhavatu : om. F} / {aham E} adyaprabhṛti madyaniṣevaṇān nivṛtto 'smi /
children.translated_text: — How does the fault of liquor thus transfer itself to me! So be it, so be it! From this day forth I abstain from the consumption of liquor!

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! mā mā mama kāraṇādo vadabhaṅgeṇa tavo khaṇḍeduṃ /
[{bhagavan! mā mā mama : mā mā evaṃ bhagavan mama G} kāraṇād vratabhaṅgena tapaḥ khaṇḍayitum /] (pādayoḥ patati /)
children.translated_text: — My lord! No, no! Do not on my account break your vow and destroy your <s>tapas</s> (austerity)! (She falls at his feet.)

children.text: - (saharṣam {utthāpyāliṅgya : utthāpyāliḍya ca CDE)} {dhṛrṇa dhṛrṇa : dhṛṣṇa dhṛṣṇa D : dhirṇa dhirṇa EG} namaḥ śivāya / priye!
children.translated_text: (With delight, raising and embracing her) Courage! Courage! Obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>! Beloved!

children.text:
peyā surā priyatamāmukham īkṣitavyaṃ
grāhyaḥ svabhāvalalito vikṛtaś ca veṣaḥ /
yenedam īdṛśam adṛśyata mokṣavartma
dīrghāyur astu bhagavān sa pinākapāṇiḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Wine is to be drunk, the beloved's face is to be gazed upon, an outfit naturally graceful yet eccentric is to be worn — may He, the lord <s>Pinākapāṇi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> bow), who revealed such a path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), have long life! ||7||

children.text: - bhaavaṃ! ṇaṃ tahā bhaṇidavvaṃ / aghante mokkhamaggaṃ aṇṇahā vaṇṇaanti / [bhagavan! nanu tathā bhaṇitavyam / arhanto {mokṣamārgam anyathā : anyathā mokṣamārga G (note ambiguous)} varṇayanti / ]
children.translated_text: — My lord! That is not how it should be said. The <s>Arhat</s>s describe the path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) differently.
— Good woman! They are indeed holders of false views. For —

children.text:
kāryasya niḥsaṃśayam ātmahetoḥ
sarūpatāṃ hetubhir abhyupetya /
duḥkhasya kāryaṃ sukham āmanantaḥ
svenaiva vākyena hatā varākāḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: Having undoubtedly accepted that the effect shares the same nature as its causes for the purpose of the self, yet declaring pleasure to be the product of suffering — the wretches are slain by their own doctrine! ||8||

children.text: - śāntaṃ śāntaṃ pāpam / na khalu te pāpā ākṣepamukhenāpy abhidhātum arhanti, ye brahmacaryakeśanirloṭana{maladhāraṇa : om. F}bhojanavelāniyama{malinapaṭa : dikpaṭa D}paridhānādibhiḥ prāṇinaḥ parikleśayanti / tadidānīṃ kutīrthasaṅkīrtanopahatāṃ jihvāṃ surayā prakṣālayitum icchāmi /
children.translated_text: — Peace, peace — sin! Those sinners are not even worth criticizing, who torment living beings through celibacy, hair-plucking, wearing filth, rules about mealtimes, wearing dirty rags, and the like. Now, having purified my tongue, defiled by the mention of wretched holy places...

children.text:
- teṇa hi aṇṇaṃ {dāṇiṃ S : dāṇi U} surāpaṇaṃ gcchāmo /
[tena hy anyam idānīṃ surāpāṇaṃ gacchāvaḥ /]
children.translated_text:
— Then let us go to another tavern now.
[Then let us go to another tavern now.]

children.text:
- priye! {tathāstu / : tathāstu / kāñcī... (? C)}
({ubhau : om. (C?)} parikrāmataḥ /)
children.translated_text:
— Beloved! So be it.
(Both walk about.)

children.text: - aho tu khalu vimānaśikharaviśrāntaghanarasitasandigdhamṛdaṅgaśabdasya madhusamayanirmāṇamātṛkāyamāṇamālyāpaṇasya kusumaśaravijayaghoṣaṇāyamānavarayuvatikāñcīravasya {kāñcīpurasya : om. H} parā vibhūtiḥ / api ca -
children.translated_text: — Ah, what surpassing glory has this city of <s>Kāñcī</s> — where the sound of drums, mistaken for the rumbling of clouds resting on the peaks of palaces, [is heard]; where the garland-shops seem to be the very workshops of Spring's creation; where the jingling of the girdle-ornaments of the finest young women seems a proclamation of the victory of the god of Love! And moreover —

children.text:
anatiśayam anantaṃ saukhyam apratyanīkaṃ
samadhigatasatattvā menire yan munīndrāḥ /
tad iha niravaśeṣaṃ dṛṣṭam etat tu citraṃ
yad uta karaṇabhogyaṃ kāmabhogātmakaṃ ca // 9 //
children.translated_text:
That unsurpassable, infinite, unopposed bliss
which the greatest sages, having realized its true nature, esteemed —
that is here seen in its entirety. But the wonder is this:
that it is enjoyed by the senses, consisting of sensual pleasure! (9)

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! bhaavadī vāruṇī via aṇavagīamahurā kañcī /
[bhagavan! bhagavatī vāruṇīvānavagītamadhurā kāñcī /]
children.translated_text:
— My lord! <s>Kāñcī</s> is like the goddess <s>Vāruṇī</s> (Liquor) — sweet beyond all song!
[My lord! <s>Kāñcī</s> is like the goddess <s>Vāruṇī</s> — sweet beyond all song!]

children.text: - priye! paśya paśya / eṣa surāpaṇo yajñavāṭavibhūtim anukaroti / {atra hi : tatra E} dhvajastambho yūpaḥ, surā somaḥ, śauṇḍā ṛtvijaḥ, caṣakāś camasāḥ, śūlyamāṃsaprabhṛtaya upadaṃśā havir viśeṣāḥ, mattavacanāni yajūṃsi, gītāni sāmāni, udaṅkāḥ sruvāḥ, tarṣo 'gniḥ, surāpaṇādhipatir yajamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: — Beloved! Look, look! This tavern imitates the splendor of a sacrificial enclosure! For here the flagstaff is the sacrificial post, liquor is the <s>Soma</s>, drunkards are the priests, cups are the <s>camasas</s> (ladles), roasted meat and the like are the special oblations, drunken speech is the <s>Yajus</s> formulae, songs are the <s>Sāman</s> chants, pitchers are the offering-spoons...

children.text:
- ahmāaṃ pi ettha bhikkhā ruddabhāo bhavissadi /
[āvayor apy atra bhikṣā {rudrabhāgo : vibhāgaḥ G} bhaviṣyati /]
children.translated_text:
— For us too, there will be <s>Rudra</s>'s share of alms here!
[For us too, there will be a share of alms here!]

children.text: - aho darśanīyāni prahata{mardala : maddala CDE}{karaṇānugatāni : karaṇāhitāni F : karaṇāhatāni C} vividhāṅgahāravacanabhrūvikārāṇi ucchritaikahastāvalambitottarīyāṇi {vigalita : vigalitāni E}vasanapratisamādhānakṣaṇaviṣamitalayāni vyākulitakaṇṭhaguṇāni mattavilāsanṛttāni /
children.translated_text: — Ah, what a sight to behold! The dances of the drunkards — accompanied by the beaten <s>mardala</s> drum, with varied gestures, expressions, and brow-movements; one hand raised holding the upper garment; interrupted by moments of readjusting their slipping clothes, with unsteady rhythm; necklaces in disarray...

children.text:
- aho rasio khu āayyo /
[aho rasikaḥ khalv ācāryaḥ /]
children.translated_text:
— Ah, what a connoisseur the master is indeed!
[Ah, what a connoisseur the master is indeed!]

children.text: - eṣā bhagavatī vāruṇī caṣakeṣv āvarjitā pratyādeśo maṇḍanānām, anunayaḥ praṇayakupitānāṃ, parākramo yauvanasya, jīvitaṃ vibhramānām / kiṃ bahunā -
children.translated_text: — This blessed goddess <s>Vāruṇī</s> (Liquor), poured into cups, is the reproach of ornaments, the conciliation of lovers' quarrels, the heroism of youth, the very life of amorous play! In short —

children.text:
mithyā trilocanavilocanapāvakena
bhasmīkṛtāṃ madanamūrtim udāharanti /
snehātmikā tadabhitāpavaśād vilīnā
seyaṃ priye! madayati prasabhaṃ manāṃsi // 10 //
children.translated_text:
They falsely say that <s>Madana</s>'s (Love's) form
was burnt to ashes by the fire of the three-eyed one's (<s>Śiva</s>'s) eye.
[In truth,] she who is the essence of passion, melted by that heat,
is this very one, O beloved, who now intoxicates our minds! (10)

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! jujjai edaṃ / ṇa hi loovaāraṇirado loaṇāho loaṃ viṇāsedi /
[bhagavan! yujyata etat / na hi lokopakāranirato lokanātho lokaṃ vināśayati /]
(ubhau kapolapaṭahaṃ kurutaḥ /)
children.translated_text:
— My lord! That makes sense. For the Lord of the World, devoted to the welfare of the world, does not destroy the world.
[My lord! That is fitting. For the Lord of the World, devoted to the welfare of the world, does not destroy the world.]
(Both slap their cheeks [in the manner of drunkards].)

children.text:
- bhavati! bhikṣāṃ dehi /
(nepathye) bhaavaṃ! esā bhikkhā / paḍigaṇhadu bhaavaṃ /
[bhagavan! eṣā bhikṣā / pratigṛhṇātu {bhagavān : om. F : bhavān G} /]
children.translated_text:
— Madam! Give us alms!
(From offstage:) My lord! Here are alms. Please accept, my lord!
[My lord! Here are alms. Let the lord accept!]

children.text: - {eṣa : eṣa eṣa CDE} pratigṛhṇāmi / priye! kva me kapālam /
children.translated_text: — Here, I accept! Beloved! Where is my skull-bowl?

children.text:
- ahaṃ vi ṇa pekkhāmi /
[aham api na paśyāmi /]
children.translated_text:
— I too do not see it.
[I too do not see it.]

children.text: - (dhyātvā) ā, tasminn eva surāpaṇe vismṛtam iti tarkayāmi / bhavatu, pratinivṛtya drakṣyāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: — (Reflecting) Ah, I surmise it was left forgotten in that very tavern. Very well, let us go back and see.

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! adhammo khu eso ādarovaṇīdāe bhikkhāe appaḍiggaho / kiṃ {dāṇi S : dāṇī U} karamha /
[bhagavan! adharmaḥ khalv eṣa ādaropanītāyā bhikṣāyā apratigrahaḥ / kim idānīṃ kurvaḥ /]
children.translated_text:
— My lord! It is indeed sinful not to accept alms offered with respect. What shall we do now?
[My lord! It is indeed sinful not to accept alms that have been respectfully offered. What shall we do now?]
— Beloved! Taking the emergency-<s>dharma</s> as authority, let it be received in a cow-horn!

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! taha /
[bhagavan! tathā /] (pratigṛhṇāti /)
(ubhau {tathā kṛtvā E} parikramyāvalokayataḥ /)
children.translated_text:
— My lord! So be it.
[My lord! So be it.] (She accepts.)
(Both walk about, looking around.)

children.text: - katham ihāpi na dṛśyate / (viṣādaṃ rūpayitvā) bho bho māheśvarāḥ! māheśvarāḥ! asmadīyaṃ bhikṣābhājanam iha bhavadbhiḥ kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ / {(karṇan dattvā E)} kim āhur bhavantaḥ - na khalu vayaṃ pāśyāma iti / hā hato 'smi / bhraṣṭaṃ me tapaḥ / kenāham idānīṃ kapālī bhaviṣyāmi / bhoḥ! kaṣṭam /
children.translated_text: — What! It is not seen here either! (Displaying distress) Ho, ho! <s>Māheśvaras</s>! <s>Māheśvaras</s>! Has our alms-vessel been seen by you here? What do you say? — 'We do not see it'? — Alas! I am ruined! My asceticism is destroyed! By what shall I now...

children.text:
yena mama pānabhojana-
śayaneṣu nitāntam upakṛtaṃ śucinā /
tasyādya māṃ viyogaḥ
sanmitrasyeva pīḍayati // 11 //
children.translated_text:
That pure [vessel] which served me so well
in drinking, eating, and sleeping —
its separation from me today
torments me like [parting from] a true friend. (11)

children.text: (patitaḥ śirastāḍanaṃ rūpayitvā) bhavatu / asti lakṣaṇamātram / na mukto 'smi kapāli{saṃjñāyāḥ : saṃjñayā Kha} / (uttiṣṭhati /)
children.translated_text: (Having fallen and acted out beating his head) Very well. There is at least the mark [of being a <s>Kapālī</s>]. I am not freed from the designation '<s>Kapālī</s>' (Skull-bearer)! (He rises.)

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! keṇa khu gahīḍaṃ kavālaṃ /
[bhagavan! kena khalu gṛhītaṃ kapālam {bhavet G} /]
children.translated_text:
— My lord! Who might have taken the skull-bowl?
[My lord! By whom might the skull-bowl have been taken?]

children.text: - priye! tarkayāmi śūlyamāṃsagarbhatvāc chunā vā śākyabhikṣunā veti /
children.translated_text: — Beloved! I suspect — since it was full of roasted meat — either by a dog or by a Buddhist monk!

children.text:
- teṇa hi aṇṇesaṇaṇimittaṃ savvaṃ {kañcīuraṃ : kañcīpuram CF} paribbhamāmo /
[tena hy anveṣaṇanimittaṃ sarvaṃ kāñcīpuraṃ paribhramāvaḥ /]
children.translated_text:
— Then let us wander through all of <s>Kāñcīpura</s> in search of it!
[Then let us roam through all of <s>Kāñcīpura</s> to search for it!]

— Beloved! So be it.
(Both walk about.)
(Then enters the Buddhist monk, bowl in hand.)

children.text:
- aho {uvāsaassa : uvāghaassa Ka(5)A(6)} dhaṇadāsaseṭṭhiṇo {mahā F}savvāvāsamahādāṇamahimāṇo, jahiṃ mae abhimadavaṇṇagandharaso macchamaṃsappaārabahulo aaṃ piṇḍavādo samāsādido / jāva dāṇi rāavihāraṃ evva gacchāmi / (parikramya ātmagatam) bhoḥ! paramakāruṇieṇa bhaavadā tahāgaeṇa pāsādesu vāso, {suvihi(a)sayyesu S : suvihiasayyesu U : suvihidasayyesu C : suvihisayyesu F(7)} pajjaṅkesu saaṇaṃ, puvvaṇhe bhoaṇaṃ, avaraṇhe surasāṇi pāṇaāṇi, {pañcasuga(ndhavvo?ndhova)hiaṃ S : pañcasugandhavodhiaṃ Ka : pañcasugandhobodhiaṃ AF : pañcasugandhavvo CD} {tambollaṃ : tambullaṃ CD}, saṇhavasaṇaparighāṇaṃ ti edehi uvadesehi bhikkhusaṅghassa aṇuggahaṃ karanteṇa kiṇṇu {hu : khu C} itthiāpariggaho surāvāṇavihāṇaṃ ca ṇa diṭṭhaṃ / ahava kahaṃ savvañco edaṃ ṇa pekkhadi / avassaṃ edehi duṭṭhabuddhatthavirehi ṇirucchāehi ahmāṇaṃ taruṇajaṇānaṃ macchareṇa piḍaaputthaesu itthiāsurāvāṇa{vihāṇāṇi : vaaṇāṇi KhaB} palāmiṭṭhāṇi tti takkemi / kahiṃ ṇu hu aviṇaṭṭhamūlapāṭhaṃ samāsādaeaṃ / tado sampuṇṇaṃ buddhavaaṇaṃ loe paāsaanto saṅghovaāraṃ karissaṃ / (parikrāmati)
[{(gandham āghrāya E)} aho upāsakasya dhanadāsaśreṣṭhinaḥ sarvāvāsamahādānamahimā, yasmin mayābhimatavarṇagandharaso matsyamāṃsaprakārabahulo 'yaṃ piṇḍapātaḥ samāsāditaḥ / yāvad idānīṃ rājavihāram eva gacchāmi / bhoḥ! paramakāruṇikena bhagavatā tathāgatena prāsādeṣu vāsaḥ, suvihitaśayyeṣu paryaṅkeṣu śayanaṃ, pūrvāhṇe bhojanam, aparāhṇe surasāni pānakāni, pañca{sugandhopahitaṃ : sugandhodbodhitaṃ G} tāmbūlaṃ, ślakṣṇavasanaparidhānam ity etair upadeśair bhikṣusaṅghasyānugrahaṃ kurvatā khin nu khalu strīparigrahaḥ {surāpānavidhānaṃ : surāpānaṃ G} ca na dṛṣṭam / atha vā kathaṃ sarvajña etan na {paśyati : prekṣiṣyati G} / avaśyam etair duṣṭabuddhasthavirair nirutsāhair asmākaṃ taruṇajanānāṃ matsareṇa piṭakapustakeṣu strīsurāpāna{vidhānāni : vacanāni G} parāmṛṣṭānīti tarkayāmi / kutra nu khalv avinaṣṭamūlapāṭhaṃ samāsādayeyam / tataḥ sampūrṇaṃ buddhavacanaṃ loke prakāśayan saṅghopakāraṃ kariṣyāmi /]
children.translated_text: — Ah, what glory of the great universal lodging-house of the merchant <s>Dhanadāsa</s>, the donor! Where I have obtained this alms-round, abundant with fish, meat, and other delicacies, rich in color, fragrance, and taste, gratifying to the point of intoxication! Now let me go to the royal monastery. (Walking about, to himself) Ah! Supreme...

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! pekkha pekkha / eso rattapaḍo imassiṃ vissatthapurisasampāde rāamagge saṅkuidasavvaṅgo ubhayapakkhasañcāridadiṭṭhī saṅkidapadavikkhevo {turiaturiaṃ S : turiaturio S v.l. : turiaṃ U : turio BD} gacchai /
[bhagavan! paśya paśya / eṣa raktapaṭo 'smin viśvastapuruṣa{sampāte : sañcāre G} rājamārge saṅkucitasarvāṅga ubhayapakṣasañcāritadṛṣṭiḥ śaṅkitapadavikṣepas tvaritatvaritaṃ gacchati /]
children.translated_text: <s>Devasomā</s>: Lord! Look, look! This one in a red robe, on this royal highway frequented by trustworthy people, with all limbs contracted, glancing to both sides, with hesitant steps, goes hurrying along.

children.text: - priye! evam etat / api cāsya haste cīvarāntaḥpracchāditaṃ kim apy astīva /
children.translated_text: Beloved! It is so. Moreover, there is something in his hand, concealed within the folds of his robe.

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! teṇa hi {olambia : avila S v.l. BCD)} āsādia jānīmo /
[bhagavan! tena hy {avalambyāsādya : avalambitaṃ samāsādya G} jānīvaḥ /]
children.translated_text: Lord! Then let us follow and accost [him] — we shall find out.

children.text: - bhavati! tathā / ({upagamya : ubhāv anugamya D}) bho bhikṣo! tiṣṭha /
children.translated_text: Good lady! Very well. (Approaching) Ho, monk! Stop.

children.text:
- ko ṇu khu maṃ evaṃ bhaṇādi / (nivṛtyāvalokya) ai ayaṃ eaṃvvavāsī duṭṭhakavālio / bhodu, imassa surāvibbhamassa lakkhaṃ ṇa homi / ({satvaraṃ : tvarito KhaBCD} gacchati /)
[ko nu khalu mām evaṃ bhaṇati / ayi ayam ekāmravāsī duṣṭa{kāpālikaḥ : kapālī G} / bhavatu, asya surāvibhramasya lakṣyaṃ na bhavāmi /]
children.translated_text: Who indeed addresses me thus? (Turning and looking) Ah, this is that wicked <s>Kāpālika</s> who dwells at the mango grove! So be it — I shall not be a target for this liquor-crazed fellow. (He goes hurriedly.)

children.text: - priye! hanta labdhaṃ kapālaṃ / asya hi maddarśanajanitabhayāt tvaraiva cauryasākṣitvaṃ pratipannā / (drutam upagamyāgrato ruṇaddhi / āḥ dhūrtta! {kvedānīṃ gamiṣyasi : om. C} /)
children.translated_text: Beloved! Ha, the skull-bowl is found! For his very haste, born of fear at seeing me, has confirmed his guilt as a thief. (Approaching quickly, he blocks his path.) Ah, scoundrel! Where will you go now?

children.text: - kavāliāusa! mā mā evaṃ / kiṃ edaṃ / (ātmagatam) aho laliarūvā uvāsiā / [kāpālikopāsika! {mā maivam : mā maivaṃ vaktum G : om. CF} / kim etat / aho lalitarūpā upāsikā /]
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāpālika</s> devotee! Don't, don't do this! What is this? (Aside) Ah, what a lovely devotee!

children.text: - bho bhikṣo! darśaya {bhavān H} tāvat / yāvad etat te pāṇau {cīvarāntaḥpracchāditaṃ : cīvarāntaritaṃ C} draṣtum icchāmi /
children.translated_text: Ho, monk! Show me then. I wish to see what you have concealed within your robe in your hand.

children.text:
- kiṃ ettha pekkhidavvaṃ / bhikkhābhāaṇaṃ khu edaṃ /
[kim atra draṣṭavyam / bhikṣābhājanaṃ khalv etat /]
children.translated_text: What is there to see here? This is merely my begging-bowl.
That is precisely why I wish to see it.

children.text:
- ā, usa! mā mā evaṃ / pacchaṇṇaṃ khu edaṃ ṇedavvaṃ /
[ā, upāsaka! mā maivam / pracchannaṃ khalv etan netavyam /]
children.translated_text: Ah, devotee! Don't, don't do this! This must be kept concealed.
No doubt the <s>Buddha</s> prescribed the wearing of many robes for the very purpose of concealing things like this!

children.text: - idaṃ {tat : om. DG} {saṃvṛtasatyam : saṃvṛṭhaṃ satyam G : saṃvṛtaṃ paramasatyam D} / paramārthasatyaṃ śrotum icchāmi /
children.translated_text: That is the 'concealed truth' (<s>saṃvṛta-satya</s>). I wish to hear the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha-satya</s>)!

children.text: - bhodu ettao parihāso / adikkamadi bhikkhāvelā / sāhemi ahaṃ / (pratiṣṭhate /) [bhavatv etāvān parihāsaḥ / atikrāmati bhikṣāvelā / sādhayāmy aham /]
children.translated_text: Enough of this joking! The begging hour is passing. I shall be on my way. (He sets off.)

children.text: - {āḥ : haḥ G}, dhūrtta! kva gamiṣyasi / dīyatāṃ me kapālam / (cīvarāntam {ālambate : avalambate CDE} /)
children.translated_text: Ah, scoundrel! Where will you go? Give me my skull-bowl! (He grasps the edge of his robe.)

children.text: - namaḥ karapaṭāyeti vaktavyaṃ, yena coraśāstraṃ praṇītam / athavā kharapaṭād apy asminn adhikāre buddha evādhikaḥ / kutaḥ -
children.translated_text: 'Homage to <s>Karapaṭa</s> (the Ass-Blanket)!' is what you should say — by whom the science of thievery was composed! Or rather, in this matter of theft, the <s>Buddha</s> is even superior to <s>Karapaṭa</s>. For —

children.text:
vedāntebhyo gṛhītvārthān
yo mahābhāratād api /
viprāṇāṃ miṣatām eva
kṛtavān kośasañcayam // 12 //
children.translated_text: Having taken materials from the <s>Vedāntas</s> and also from the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, while the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> looked on, he made a collection of treasure. [verse 12]

children.text:
- santaṃ pāpaṃ santaṃ pāpaṃ /
[śāntaṃ {pāpaṃ : om. G} śāntaṃ pāpaṃ /]
children.translated_text: May the sin be quelled! May the sin be quelled!

children.text: - evaṃ suvṛttasya tapasvinaḥ katham iva pāpaṃ na śāmyati /
children.translated_text: How indeed can sin not be quelled for such a well-behaved ascetic?

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! parissanto via lakkhīasi / ṇa edaṃ suhovāasulahaṃ kavālaṃ / tā edinā gosiṅgeṇa suraṃ pibia jādabalo bhavia imiṇā saha vivādaṃ karehi /
[bhagavan! pariśrānta iva lakṣyase / naitat sukhopāyasulabhaṃ kapālaṃ / tad etena gośṛṅgeṇa surāṃ pītvā jātabalo bhūtvānena saha vivādaṃ kuru /]
children.translated_text: Lord! You seem exhausted. That skull-bowl is not easily obtainable by gentle means. So drink some liquor from this cow-horn, and having gained strength, quarrel with this fellow.
So be it! (<s>Devasomā</s> gives liquor to the <s>Kapālī</s>.)
(Having drunk) Beloved! You too must relieve your fatigue.

children.text: - ayam asmākam apakārī / saṃvibhāgapradhānaḥ svasiddhāntaḥ {pramāṇayitavyaḥ C} / śeṣam ācāryāya pradīyatām /
children.translated_text: This fellow has wronged us. The principal [tenet] of our doctrine is sharing. Let the remainder be given to the teacher.

children.text:
- jaṃ bhaavaṃ āṇavedi / gahṇadu bhaavaṃ /
[yad bhagavān ājñāpayati / gṛḥṇātu {bhagavān : bhavān G} /]
children.translated_text: As the lord commands. Let the lord take it.

children.text:
- (ātmagatam) aho suhovaṇado abbhudao / ettao doso - mahājaṇo pekkhissadi / (prakāśam) bhodi / mā mā evaṃ / ṇa {vaḍḍhadi : vaddhai KaA} ahmāṇaṃ / (sṛkvaṇī leḍhi /)
[aho sukhopanato 'bhyudayaḥ / etāvān {atra khalu eṣa G} doṣaḥ - mahājano drakṣyati / bhavati / mā maivam / na vardhate 'smākam /]
children.translated_text: (Aside) Ah, what a stroke of good fortune presenting itself! The only drawback is — the public will see. (Aloud) Good lady! Don't, don't do that! It does not befit us. (He licks his lips.)

children.text:
- dhaṃsa / kudo de ettiāṇi bhāadheāṇi /
[{dhvaṃsasva : duṣṭa G} / kutas te {etāvanti : etāni G} bhāgadheyāni /]
children.translated_text: Get lost! How can you have so many shares?

children.text: - priye! iyam asyecchāvirodhinī vāg mukhaprasekena skhala(ya?)ti (8) /
children.translated_text: Beloved! These words of his, opposing [his own] desire, stumble from the wetness of his mouth.

children.text:
- idāṇiṃ vi ṇatthi de karuṇā /
[idānīm api { nāsti te : te nāsti G} karuṇā /]
children.translated_text: Even now you have no compassion!

children.text: - yady asti karuṇā, kathaṃ vītarāgo bhaviṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: If I have compassion, how will I become free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>)?

children.text:
- evaṃ vīdarāgiṇā vīdaroseṇa vi hodavvaṃ /
[evaṃ vītarāgiṇā vītaroṣeṇāpi bhavitavyam /]
children.translated_text: One who is free from passion should also be free from anger.

children.text: - vītaroṣo bhaviṣyāmi, yadi me svakaṃ dāsyati /
children.translated_text: I will become free from anger, if he gives me my property.

children.text: - kathaṃ kapālam ity āha / athavā yuktam etat /
children.translated_text: 'What skull-bowl?' he says! Or rather, that is fitting —

children.text:
dṛṣṭāni vastūni mahīsamudra-
mahīdharādīni mahānti mohāt /
apahnuvānasya sutaḥ kathaṃ tvam
alpam na nihnotum alaṃ kapālam // 13 //
children.translated_text: You who, out of delusion, deny having seen great things such as the earth, the oceans, the mountains, and the like — how are you, O son, not able to deny a small skull-bowl? [verse 13]

children.text: - bhaavaṃ! kevalaṃ lālīyamāṇo ṇa daissadi / tā edassa hatthādo ācchindia gacchāmo / [bhagavan! kevalaṃ lālyamāno na dāsyati / tad etasya hastād ācchidya gacchāvaḥ /]
children.translated_text: Lord! He will not give it simply by being coaxed. So let us snatch it from his hand and go.
Beloved! Very well. (They endeavor to snatch it.)

children.text: - dhaṃsa duṭṭhakavālia / (hastena nudan pādena {tāḍayati : pātayati D} /) [{dhvaṃsasva : dhvaṃsa (9) gaccha G} duṣṭakāpālika!]
children.translated_text: Get lost, wicked <s>Kāpālika</s>! (Pushing with his hand, he kicks [him] down.)

children.text: - mudo si dāsievutta! ({keśāpakarśaṇaṃ : keśākarśaṇaṃ D} rūpayitvā nirālambanā patitā /) [mṛto 'si dāsyāḥputra!]
children.translated_text: You are dead, son of a slave-woman! (Miming hair-pulling, she falls without support.)

children.text:
- (ātmagatam) aghaṃ buddhassa viṇṇāṇaṃ, jeṇa muṇḍaṇaṃ {diṭṭhaṃ : kidaṃ KaA} / (prakāśam) uṭṭhehi uṭṭhehi usie! uṭṭhehi / (iti devasomām {utthāpayati : hastena gṛhṇāti E} /)
[arhaṃ {(arghaṃ vā) S: (aghaṃ vā) U} buddhasya vijñānam, yena muṇḍanaṃ dṛṣṭam / uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha upāsike uttiṣṭha /]
children.translated_text: (Aside) Precious is the wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s>, by which the tonsure was ordained! (Aloud) Get up, get up, devotee! Get up! (He lifts up <s>Devasomā</s>.)

children.text: - paśyantu paśyantu māheśvarāḥ anena duṣṭabhikṣunāmadhārakeṇa nāgasenena mama priyatamāpāṇigrahaṇaṃ kriyamāṇam /
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Māheśvaras</s> look! By this wicked one who merely bears the name of a monk — this <s>Nāgasena</s> — the hand of my beloved is being seized!

children.text:
- ā vusa! mā mā evaṃ / dhammo khu ahmāṇaṃ visamapadidāṇukampā /
[ā upāsaka! {(āyuṣman! vā) SU} mā maivam / dharmaḥ khalv {ayam G} asmākaṃ {viṣamapatitānukampā : viṣamapatitānām anukampā G} /]
children.translated_text: Ah, devotee! Don't say that! Our <s>dharma</s> is compassion for those who have fallen into misfortune.

children.text:
- kim ayam api sarvajñadharmaḥ / nanv ahaṃ pūrvaṃ patito 'smi / bhavatu, kim anena / idānīṃ tava śiraḥkapālaṃ mama bhikṣākapālaṃ bhaviṣyati /
(sarve kalahaṃ {rūpayanti : kurvanti C} /)
children.translated_text: Is this too the <s>dharma</s> of the Omniscient One? Was I not the one who fell first? So be it, what of this? Now your skull shall become my begging skull-bowl! (All engage in a brawl.)

children.text: - paśyantu paśyantu māheśvarāḥ / eṣa duṣṭabhikṣunāmadhārako {nāgaseno DF} mama bhikṣākapālaṃ muṣitvā svayam evākrandati / bhavatu, aham apy ākrośayiṣye / abrahmaṇyam abrahmaṇyam /
children.translated_text: Look, look, O <s>Māheśvaras</s>! This wicked one bearing the name of a Buddhist monk, <s>Nāgasena</s>, having stolen my begging-skull, himself cries out! So be it — I too shall raise a cry! Injustice! Injustice!

children.text: - bho babhrukalpa! duṣṭabhikṣunāmadhārako nāgaseno mama bhikṣākapālaṃ corayitvā dātuṃ necchati /
children.translated_text: O <s>Babhrukalpa</s>! This wicked one bearing the name of a Buddhist monk, <s>Nāgasena</s>, having stolen my begging-skull, does not wish to give it back!

children.text: - (ātmagatam) {aye! D} yad asmābhir anuṣṭheyaṃ, gandharvaiḥ tad anuṣṭhitam / eṣa durātmā,
children.translated_text: (Aside) Ah! What we ought to have done, the <s>Gandharvas</s> have done! This wretch,

children.text:
tāṃ kṣaurikasya dāsīṃ
mama dayitāṃ cīvarāntadarśitayā /
ākarṣati kākaṇyā
bahuśo {gāṃ : gaḥ E} grāsamuṣṭyeva // 14 //
children.translated_text: By a <s>kākaṇī</s> (small coin) shown from within his robe, he lures that slave-girl of the barber, my beloved, repeatedly — as [one lures] a cow with a handful of grain. // 14 //

children.text: tad idānīṃ pratihastiprotsāhanena {asmat G}śatrupakṣaṃ dhvaṃsayāmi / (prakāśam) bho nāgasena! apy evam etad, yathāyam āha /
children.translated_text: So now, by encouraging the opposing elephant, I shall destroy the enemy's flank! (Aloud) O <s>Nāgasena</s>! Is it so, as this man says?

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! tuvaṃ pi evaṃ bhaṇāsi / ādiṇṇādāṇā veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / mudhāvādā veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / {abbamhacayyā : abbamhaññacayyā (Ka)(10)A} veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / pāṇādipādā veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / {akālabhoaṇā : bhoaṇakālattherā KaAF} veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / ahmāaṃ buddhadhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi /
[bhagavan! tvam {apy evaṃ bhaṇasi : api na jānāsi G} / adattādānād viramanaṃ śikṣāpadam / mṛṣāvādād viramanaṃ śikṣāpadam / abrahmacaryād viramanaṃ śikṣāpadam / prāṇātipātād viramanaṃ śikṣāpadam / akālabhojanād viramanaṃ śikṣāpadam / asmākaṃ {buddhadharmaṃ : buddhaṃ dharmaṃ G} śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi /]
children.translated_text: Sir! You too speak thus? 'Abstention from taking what is not given' is a training rule. 'Abstention from false speech' is a training rule. 'Abstention from unchastity' is a training rule. 'Abstention from taking life' is a training rule. 'Abstention from eating at the wrong time' is a training rule. I take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: - satyasoma! īdṛśa eṣāṃ samayaḥ / kim atra prativacanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Satyasoma</s>! Such is their code. What answer is there to this?

children.text: - nanv asmākam anṛtaṃ na vaktavyam iti samayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why, our code too is that we must not speak an untruth!

children.text: - ubhayam apy upapannam / ko {'tra : om. D} nirṇayopāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Both [statements] are warranted. What means of decision is there?

children.text: - buddhavaaṇaṃ pamāṇīkaraanto bhikkhū surābhāaṇaṃ gaṇhadi tti ko ettha hedū / [{bho G} buddhavacanaṃ pramāṇīkurvan bhikṣuḥ surābhājanaṃ gṛhṇātīti ko 'tra hetuḥ /]
children.translated_text: What reason is there that a monk who takes the word of the <s>Buddha</s> as authority would take hold of a liquor vessel?
A mere assertion does not prove the case for a logician.
Where there is direct perception, talk of logical proof is meaningless.

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! edassa hatthe civarāntappacchādidaṃ kavālaṃ /
[bhagavan! etasya haste cīvarāntaḥpracchāditaṃ kapālam /]
children.translated_text: Sir! The skull is in his hand, concealed within his robe!

children.text:
- bho bhaavaṃ! edaṃ kavālaṃ ṇa parakeraaṃ /
[bho bhagavan! etat kapālaṃ na parakīyam /]
children.translated_text: O sir! This skull is not someone else's!

children.text: - paśyantu paśyantu māheśvarāḥ kāpālikena {kapāline KaAF} kṛtam anyāyyam asya bhadantasya sādhuvṛttatāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Look, look, O <s>Māheśvaras</s>! [See] the injustice done by a <s>Kāpālika</s>, and [see] the virtuous conduct of this reverend one!

children.text:
- ādiṇṇādāṇā veramaṇaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ / {... (iti punas tad eva paṭhati /) : KaACD repeat the whole passage}
({ityādi paṭhitvā E} ubhau nṛtyataḥ /)
children.translated_text: 'Abstention from taking what is not given' is a training rule... (He recites the same passage again.) (Both dance.)

children.text:
- haddhi / {lajjitavve : udidavve C} kāle ṇaccadi /
[hā dhik / lajjitavye kāle nṛtyati /]
children.translated_text: Alas! He dances at a time when he should be ashamed!

children.text: - āḥ ko nṛtyati / (sarvato vilokya {ātmagatam R} /) ā mama naṣṭabhikṣābhājana{darśana : janita H}kutūhalamalayānilaprayuktāyā dhruvam asya nṛttabuddhiḥ prītilatāyā vilasiteṣu /
children.translated_text: Ha! Who is dancing? (Looking around, aside) Ah — surely this urge to dance arose from the joy-creeper's blossoming, [stirred by] a Malaya breeze born of the curiosity of seeing my lost begging-vessel!

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! keṇa kāraṇeṇa edaṃ ṇa lakkhīadi / bho ācikkhadu bhaavaṃ / imassa aaṃ vaṇṇo /
[{bho G} bhagavan! kena kāraṇenaitan na lakṣyate / bhoḥ ācaṣṭāṃ bhagavān / asyāyaṃ varṇaḥ /]
children.translated_text: Sir! For what reason is this not noticed? Pray tell, sir! This is the color of it [my skull].

children.text: - kim atra vaktavyam / nanu mayā dṛṣṭam / kākād api kṛṣṇam idaṃ kapālam /
children.translated_text: What is there to say? I have seen it — this skull is blacker than a crow!

children.text:
- teṇa hi edaṃ mamakeraaṃ ti saaṃ eva abbhuvagadaṃ /
[tena hy etan madīyam iti svayam evābhyupagatam /]
children.translated_text: Then it is thereby admitted by yourself that this is mine!

children.text:
- satyam abhyupagataṃ tava varṇāntarakaraṇe naipuṇyam /
paśya,
children.translated_text: True — it is admitted. Your skill lies in changing the color! Look:

children.text:
yad etad āsīt prathamaṃ svabhāvato
mṛṇālabhaṅgacchavicoram ambaram /
nanu tvayā nītam acintyakarmaṇā
tad eva bālāruṇarāgatāmratām // 15 //
children.translated_text: That which at first was by nature a garment white as the gleam of a lotus stalk's fracture — was it not you, performer of inconceivable deeds, who brought it to the coppery redness of the young dawn? // 15 //
Covered outside and inside with never-departing <s>kaṣāya</s> (ochre dye / defilements),

children.text: tvāṃ prāptaṃ syāt kathaṃ nāma kapālam akaṣāyitam // 16 //
children.translated_text: How could a skull that has come to you not be dyed in <s>kaṣāya</s>? // 16 //

children.text:
- hā hadahmi mandabhāā / savvalakkhaṇasampaṇṇadāe kamalāsaṇasīsakavālāṇubhāvassa puṇṇamāsisomadaṃsaṇassa ṇiccasurāgandhiṇo edassa maliṇapaḍasaṃsaggeṇa ia īdisī avitthā saṃvuttā / (iti roditi /)
[hā hatāsmi mandabhāgā / sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannatayā {kamalāsanaśīrṣakapālānubhāvasya : om. G} paurṇamāsīsomadarśanasya nityasurāgandhina etasya malinapaṭasaṃsargeṇeyam īdṛśy avasthā saṃvṛttā /]
children.translated_text: Alas! I am slain, ill-fated that I am! Due to the perfection of all auspicious marks, [my skull] possessed the splendor of the skull atop <s>Kamalāsana</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) head; it had the appearance of the full-moon <s>Soma</s>; it always bore the fragrance of liquor — and through contact with this one's dirty cloth, it has come to such a state! (She weeps.)

children.text: - priye! alaṃ santāpena / punaḥ śucir bhaviṣyati / śrūyante hi mahānti bhūtāni prāyaścittair apanītakalmaṣāṇi bhavanti / {tathā hi : yathā C} -
children.translated_text: Beloved! Enough of grief! It will be clean again. For it is heard that even great beings have their sins removed by <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory rites). For example —

children.text:
āsthāya prayato mahāvratam idaṃ bālenducūḍāmaṇiḥ
svāmī no mumuce pitāmahaśiraśchedodbhavād enasaḥ /
nātho 'pi tridivaukasāṃ triśirasaṃ tvaṣṭus tanūjaṃ purā
hatvā yajñaśatena śāntadurito bheje punaḥ puṇyatām // 17 //
children.translated_text: Having devotedly undertaken this great vow, our Lord, whose crest-jewel is the young crescent moon, was freed from the sin born of severing the head of the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>). Even the Lord of the celestials (<s>Indra</s>), having formerly slain <s>Triśiras</s> (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>), the son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, attained purity again, his sin pacified by a hundred sacrifices. // 17 //
What has been stated is in accordance with scripture.

children.text: - {bho : bhodu C} vaṇṇo dāva mae kido / imassa saṇṭhāṇaparimāṇaṃ keṇa ṇimmidaṃ / [bhoḥ! varṇas tāvan mayā kṛtaḥ / asya saṃsthānaparimāṇaṃ {kena nirmitaṃ : tāvat katham G} /]
children.translated_text: Well, sir! The color was indeed changed by me. But who fashioned its shape and dimensions?
But surely you [Buddhists] are born from a continuity of illusion (<s>māyā</s>)!

children.text:
- kettiaṃ velaṃ bhavantaṃ akkosāmi / gaṇhadu bhaavaṃ /
[kiyantīṃ velāṃ bhavantam ākrośāmi / gṛhṇātu (11) bhagavān /]
children.translated_text: How long shall I revile you? Take it, sir!
Surely even by the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) of giving was thus fulfilled!

children.text:
- evaṃ {gade : kide F} {kiṃ S : ki U} dāṇiṃ me saraṇaṃ /
[evaṃ gate kim idānīṃ me śaraṇam /]
children.translated_text: This being the case, what is now my refuge?

children.text: - nāyaṃ vyavahāro mayā paricchettuṃ śakyate / tad adhikaraṇam eva yāsyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: This dispute cannot be settled by me. Let us go to court.

children.text:
- bhagavan! yady evaṃ, namaḥ kapālāya /
[bhaavaṃ! jai evaṃ, ṇamo kavālassa /]
children.translated_text: Sir! If so — homage to the skull!

children.text:
- eso uṇa aṇeavihārabhoasamadhigadavittasañcao jahākāmaṃ adhikaraṇakāruṇiāṇaṃ muhāṇi pūreduṃ pāredi / ahmāaṃ puṇa ahicammabhūdimattavibhavassa dariddakavāliassa pariāriāṇaṃ ko etta vibhavo adhikaraṇaṃ pavisiduṃ /
[eṣa punar anekavihārabhogasamadhigatavittasaṃcayo yathākāmam {adhikaraṇa : kāruṇa C}{kāraṇikānāṃ : kāruṇikānāṃ All mss.(12)} mukhāni pūrayituṃ pārayati / asmākaṃ punar ahicarmabhūtimātra{vibhavasya : vibhava G}daridrakāpālikasya paricārikāṇāṃ ko 'tra vibhavo 'dhikaraṇaṃ praveṣṭum / ]
children.translated_text: This one, having accumulated wealth from the revenues of many <s>vihāras</s> (monasteries), is able to fill at will the mouths of the judicial officers. But for us — the attendants of a poor <s>Kāpālika</s> whose only wealth is a snakeskin — what means have we to enter the court?

children.text:
ajihmaiḥ sāragurubhiḥ
sthiraiḥ ślakṣṇaiḥ sujanmabhiḥ /
tair dharmo dhāryate stambhaiḥ
prāsāda iva sādhubhḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: By pillars that are straight, weighty in substance, firm, smooth, and well-born — by such [pillars] is <s>Dharma</s> (justice) upheld, as a palace [is upheld] by good [pillars]. // 18 //

children.text: - kṛtam anena / kutaś cid api nyāyya{nyāya BCE}vṛtter bhayaṃ nāsti /
children.translated_text: Done with this! From one who follows a just course, there is nothing to fear.

children.text: - {(pāśupatam avalokya) D} bho bhaavaṃ! tumaṃ dāva aggado hohi {hodu ABCF} / [bho bhagavan! tvaṃ tāvad agrato bhava /]
children.translated_text: (Looking at the <s>Pāśupata</s>) O sir! You go ahead first!
Very well — the first procedure! (All walk about.)

children.text: - eśo eśo duṭṭhakukkule / śullamaṃśagabbhaṃ kavālaṃ gaṇhia dhāvaśi / dāśīevutta! kahiṃ gamiśśiśi / eśo dāṇiṃ kavālaṃ ṇikkhivia maṃ khāyidukāmo ahimuhaṃ āhāvai / (diśo vilokya) imiṇā patthaleṇa dantāṇi śe bhañjiśśaṃ / kahaṃ kavālaṃ ujjhia palāaśi / ummatte duṭṭhakukkule īdiśeṇa {ṇāma : om. F} śūlattaṇeṇa mae śaha vi lośaṃ kaleśi / gāmaśūgalaṃ āluhia gagaṇam uppadideṇa śāgaleṇa paḍipañjia lāvaṇaṃ balā gahīde śakkaśude timiṅgale / ai elaṇḍalukkha! kiṃ bhaṇāśi / aliaṃ aliaṃ tti / ṇaṃ eśe muśalaśamaviśālalambahatthe daddule me śakkhī / ahava tellokkavidiapalakkamaśśa śakkhiṇā kiṃ kayyaṃ / {evaṃ : evvaṃ dāva D} kaliśśaṃ / kukkilakhādiaśeśaṃ maṃśakhaṇḍaṃ khādiśśaṃ / (khādan bhrāntaḥ /) hā hā mālido mhi, bappheṇa mālido mhi / (ruditvā vilokya) ke eśe maṃ tāleśi / (vilokya /) duṭṭhadālaā! jaśśa vā kaśśa vā {bhāuṇeo S : bhāaṇeo U} khu ahaṃ, bhīmaśeṇaśśa ghaṭukkao via / avi a śuṇātha -
children.translated_text: <s>Unmattaka</s> (The Madman): Here, here is the wicked dog! Having seized the skull-bowl with the roasting meat inside, he runs! Son of a slave-woman! Where will you go? Now he has put down the skull-bowl and comes rushing toward me, wanting to eat me! With this stone I'll break his teeth! What! Having abandoned the skull-bowl, you flee? Mad wicked dog! With such bravery you dare quarrel even with me! [Like one who] having mounted a village pig, flew up to the sky; [like] the jackal who, having attacked, seized <s>Rāvaṇa</s> by force; [like the one who] caught <s>Timiṅgila</s>, the son of <s>Śakra</s>! Hey, castor-oil tree! What do you say? 'False, false!' — is it? Well, this frog with arms as long and broad as pestles is my witness! Or rather, what need of witnesses for one whose prowess is known throughout the three worlds? This is what I shall do — I shall eat this piece of meat, the leftover of the dog! (Eating, he wanders about.) Alas, alas! I am struck! By tears I am struck! (Weeping and looking around) Who strikes me? (Looking) Wicked boys! I am indeed the nephew of whoever — like <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, [nephew] of <s>Bhīmasena</s>! Moreover, listen —

children.text:
gahīdaśūlā bahuveśadhāliṇo
śadaṃ piśāā udale vahanti me /
śadaṃ ca vagghāṇa ṇiśaggabhīśaṇaṃ
muheṇa muñcāmi ahaṃ {maholae S : maholaye U} // 19 //
children.translated_text: A hundred <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), bearing spears and wearing many disguises,

children.text:
kahaṃ maṃ bāhanti / paśīdantu paśīdantu dālaabhaṭṭā / imaśśa maṃśakhaṇḍaśśa kālaṇādo mā maṃ bāheha / (agrato vilokya /) eśe khu amhāṇaṃ āālie śūlanandī / {jāva S : jāvaṃ U} ṇaṃ uvaśappāmi / (iti dhāvati /)
[eṣa eṣa duṣṭakukkuraḥ / śūlyamāṃsagarbhaṃ kapālaṃ gṛhītvā {dhāvasi : dhāvati G} / dāsyāḥputra! kutra gamiṣyasi / eṣa idānīṃ kapālaṃ nikṣipya māṃ khāditukāmo 'bhimukham ādhāvati / anena prastareṇa dantān asya bhaṅkṣyāmi / kathaṃ kapālam ujjhitvā palāyase / unmatto duṣṭakukkura īdṛśena nāma śūratvena {saha G} mayā {sahāpi roṣaṃ : saha virodhaṃ G} karoṣi / grāma{sūkaram : sūkaragalam G} āruhya gaganam utpatitena {sāgareṇa : (probably) śvagaṇena G(13)} {prabhañjya : pratibhañjya G} {rāvaṇaṃ balād : airāvataṃ G} gṛhītaḥ {śakrasutas : sasutas G} timiṅgilaḥ /(14) ayi eraṇḍavṛkṣa! kiṃ bhaṇasi / alīkam alīkam iti / {nanv eṣa musalasamaviśālalambahasto darduro me sākṣī : hanumata eṣā musalasamaviśālalambahaste dardure me śaktiḥ G} / {athavā trailokyaviditaparākramasya sākṣiṇā kiṃ kāryam : athavā kiṃ mama trailokyaviditaparākramasya śaktyāḥ kāryam G} / evaṃ {kariṣyāmi : tāvat kariṣye G} / kukkurakhāditaśeṣaṃ māṃsakhaṇḍaṃ khādiṣyāmi / hā hā {bāṣpeṇa mārito 'smi : mālito 'smi bāṣpeṇa G} / ka eṣa māṃ tāḍayasi / {duṣṭadārakā : duṣṭadārakabhartāra! vāsudevasya bhāgi G}! yasya vā kasya vā bhāgineyaḥ khalv ahaṃ, bhīmasenasya ghaṭotkaca iva / api ca śṛṇutha -
children.translated_text: dwell in my belly; and hundreds of serpents, naturally fearsome as tigers, I release from my mouth! [verse 19] How dare they beat me! Be gracious, be gracious, O masters of boys! Do not beat me on account of this piece of meat! (Looking ahead) Here indeed is our teacher <s>Śūranandī</s>! Let me approach him. (He runs.)
A hundred <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), bearing spears and wearing many disguises,

children.text: śataṃ piśācā udare {vahanti : vasanti G} me /

children.translated_text: and hundreds of serpents, naturally fearsome as tigers,
I release from my mouth, great serpents! [verse 19]

children.text: kathaṃ {māṃ bādhante : punar api māṃ tāḍayanti G} / prasīdantu prasīdantu dārakabhartāraḥ! asya māṃsakhaṇḍasya kāraṇād mā māṃ {bādhadhvam : tāḍayatha G} / eṣa khalv asmākam ācāryaḥ śūranandī / yāvad enam {upasarpāmi : upaharāmi G(15)}/]
children.translated_text: How dare they beat me! Be gracious, be gracious, O masters of boys! Do not beat me on account of this piece of meat! Here indeed is our teacher <s>Śūranandī</s>! Let me approach him.

children.text:
- aye! ayam unmattakaḥ ita evābhivartate / ya eṣaḥ -
nirviṣṭojjhitacitracīvaradharo rūkṣair nitāntākulaiḥ
keśair uddhatabhasma{pāṃsu : pāṇḍu D}nicayair nirmālya{mālākulaiḥ : mālāvṛtaḥ CE : mālāvṛtaiḥ D} /
children.translated_text: Ah! This madman approaches from this direction. He is — Wearing discarded motley garments, with dry and utterly tangled hair covered with heaps of ash-dust, garlanded with withered flower-garlands,

children.text:
ucchiṣṭāśanalolupair balibhujām anvāsyamāno gaṇair
bhūyān grāmakasārasañcaya iva bhrāmyan manuṣyākṛtiḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: followed by packs of dogs greedy for the leavings of food, wandering about in human form like a moving heap of village refuse. [verse 20]

children.text:
- {(pāśupatam avalokya) CDE} jāva ṇaṃ uvaśappāmi / (upasṛtya) mahāśāhuṇo caṇḍālakukkulaśśa śaāśādo ahiadaṃ edaṃ {kavālaṃ : om. D} paḍigaṇhadu bhaavaṃ /
[yāvad enam upasarpāmi / mahāsādhoś caṇḍālakukkurasya sakāśād {mayā G} adhigatam etat kapālaṃ pratigṛhṇātu {bhagavān : bhavān / bhagavan(16) / mastakena vandāmi G} /]
children.translated_text: (Seeing the <s>Pāśupata</s>) Let me approach him. (Approaching) Great sage! I have obtained this skull-bowl from the despicable dog. Let the lord accept it! I bow with my head.
(With a sidelong glance) Let it be placed in the bowl.

children.text:
- eso mahāpāsuvado edassa joggī /
[eṣa mahāpāśupata etasya yogyaḥ /] (Satyasoma!)
children.translated_text: This great <s>Pāśupata</s> is the right one for this [skull-bowl]! (<s>Satyasoma</s>!)

children.text:
- (kapālinam upagamya kapālaṃ bhūmau nikṣipya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pādayoḥ patitvā) mahādeva! kalīadu paśādo / eśo de añjalī /
[mahādeva! kriyatāṃ prasādaḥ / eṣa te 'ñjaliḥ /]
children.translated_text: (Approaching the <s>Kapālī</s>, placing the skull-bowl on the ground, circumambulating, and falling at his feet) Great God! Show grace! Here is my offering to you.

children.text: - bhagavatprasādāt punar api kapālī saṃvṛttaḥ / (grahītum icchati /)
children.translated_text: By the grace of the Lord, I have become a <s>Kapālī</s> (skull-bearer) once again! (He wishes to take it.)

children.text:
- dāśīevutta! viśaṃ khādehi /
[dāsyāḥputra! viṣaṃ khāda /]
(kapālam ācchidya gacchati /)
children.translated_text: Son of a slave-woman! Eat poison! (He snatches the skull-bowl and runs away.)

children.text: - (anusṛtya) {eṣa : hanta C : kaṣṭam eṣa E} yamapuruṣo me jīvitaṃ harati / abhyavapadyetāṃ bhavantau /
children.translated_text: (Following) This servant of <s>Yama</s> takes my very life! May you two come to my aid!

children.text:
- hodu / amhe de sahāā homa /
[bhavatu / āvāṃ te sahāyau bhavāvaḥ /]
(sarve rundhanti /)
children.translated_text: So be it! We are your allies! (All block [the madman].)

children.text:
- mūḍha! ki ṇa pekkhaśi, śuvaṇṇabhāaṇaṃ khu edaṃ /
[mūḍha! kiṃ na paśyasi, suvarṇabhājanaṃ khalv etat /]
children.translated_text: Fool! Don't you see? This is a golden vessel!
Who made such a golden vessel?

children.text:
- ediṇā śuvaṇṇavaṇṇapaḍāvudeṇa śuvaṇṇakārāvuttaeṇa kidaṃ tti bhaavaṃ / śuvaṇṇabhāaṇaṃ tti bhaṇāmi /
[etena suvarṇavarṇapaṭāvṛtena suvarṇa{kārāvuttena : kāreṇa G} kṛtam iti bhagavan / suvarṇabhājanam iti bhaṇāmi /]
children.translated_text: By this one covered with a gold-colored cloth, made by a goldsmith — thus, lord. I call it a golden vessel.

children.text:
- ummattao tti bahuśo edaṃ śaddaṃ śuṇomi / edaṃ gaṇhia daliśehi ummattaaṃ / (kapāline kapālaṃ prayachati /)
[{unmattaka iti bahuśa etaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇomi / etad gṛhītvā darśayonmattakam / : yuṣmākaṃ unmattakā / yuṣmākaṃ putrā unmattakāḥ / etad dattvā darśayāmi unmattakatvam / G}]
children.translated_text: 'Madman' — I hear this word often! Take this and show [who is] a madman! (He gives the skull-bowl to the <s>Kapālī</s>.)

children.text: - (kapālaṃ gṛhītvā) ayam idānīṃ kuḍyenāntarhitaḥ / śīghram anugamyatām /
children.translated_text: (Taking the skull-bowl) He has now disappeared behind a wall! Quickly, let him be followed!
I have received grace! (The madman exits swiftly.)

children.text:
- aho acchariaṃ / paravakkhassa lābheṇa ahaṃ parituṭṭho hmi /
[aho āścaryam / parapakṣasya lābhenāhaṃ parituṣṭo 'smi /]
children.translated_text: Ah, how wonderful! I am pleased by the gain of the opposing party!

children.text:
ciraṃ mayā caritam akhaṇḍitaṃ tapo
maheśvare bhagavati bhaktir {asti : astu C} me /
tirohitaḥ sa tu sahasā sukhena nas
tvam adya yat kuśali kapāla dṛśyase // 21 //
children.translated_text: Long have I practiced unbroken austerity, and my devotion is to the Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>. He had suddenly disappeared, but to our delight, O skull-bowl, you are seen today, safe and sound! [verse 21]

children.text:
- bhaavaṃ! candasamāgadaṃ via paosaṃ bhaavantaṃ pekkhantīe ajja āṇandadī via me diṭṭhī /
[bhagavan! candrasamāgatam iva pradoṣaṃ bhagavantaṃ paśyatyā adyānandatīva me dṛṣṭiḥ /]
children.translated_text: Lord! Like the moonrise at dusk, my eyes rejoice today at seeing the lord [reunited with the skull-bowl]!
Indeed, the good fortune is yours!

children.text: - (ātmagatam /) satyam etat / nāsty adoṣavatāṃ bhayam iti / {yad : om. CD} ayam adya {bhikṣur : om. D} vyāghramukhāt {katham api E} paribhraṣṭaḥ / (prakāśam /) yāvad aham idānīm eva suhṛdabhyudayakṛtam ānandaṃ purodhāya bhagavataḥ {pūrva : pūrvaṃ KaA(17)}{sthalī : sthala C}nivāsino {dhūma : dhūmra H}velāṃ {pratipālayāmi : sambhāvayāmi C}/ ayaṃ cādyaprabhṛti -
children.translated_text: (Aside) This is true — there is nothing to fear for those who are without fault. Today this monk has somehow slipped from the tiger's mouth! (Aloud) Now I shall, placing foremost the joy occasioned by my friend's good fortune, await the hour of twilight devotion to the Lord who formerly dwelt on the [cremation] ground. And from this day forth —

children.text:
virodhaḥ pūrvasambaddho
yuvayor astu śāśvataḥ /
parasparaprītikaraḥ
kirātārjunayor iva // 22 //
children.translated_text: May the enmity that was formerly joined between you two be everlasting — and productive of mutual affection, like [the enmity] between <s>Kirāta</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>! // 22 //

children.text: - bho nāgasena! yan mayāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ, tat prasannahṛdayaṃ tvam icchāmi /
children.translated_text: O <s>Nāgasena</s>! For whatever offense I have committed, I wish your heart to be favorably disposed.

children.text:
- kiṃ edaṃ pi abbhatthaṇīaṃ / kiṃ de piaṃ karemi /
[kim etad apy abhyarthanīyam / kiṃ te priyaṃ karomi /]
children.translated_text: Need this even be requested? What shall I do that would please you?

children.text: - yadi me bhagavān prasannaḥ, kim ataḥ param aham icchāmi /
children.translated_text: If the reverend sir is gracious toward me, what more could I wish?
I shall take my leave now.
May you go — until we meet again!

children.text: - priye devasome! gacchāvas tāvat / : om. (no siglum)(18)}

śaśvad bhūtyai prajānāṃ vahatu vidhihutām āhutiṃ jātavedā
vedān viprā bhajantāṃ surabhiduhitaro bhūridohā bhavantu /
udyuktaḥ sveṣu dharmeṣv ayam api vigatavyāpad ācandratāraṃ
rājanvān astu śaktipraśamitaripuṇā śatrumallena lokaḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Jātavedas</s> (the Fire God) convey the offering poured according to rite for the eternal prosperity of the people! May the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> cultivate the <s>Vedas</s>! May the daughters of <s>Surabhi</s> (the divine cow) yield abundant milk! May this world, zealously devoted to its own <s>dharmas</s>, free from calamity until the moon and stars endure, be ruled by <s>Śatrumalla</s> ('Wrestler of Foes,' i.e., the king), who has subdued his enemies by his might! // 23 //
The <s>Mattavilāsaprahasana</s> (The Farce of Drunken Sport) is concluded.

children.translated_text: End notes: (1) Note by <s>Sastri</s>, also printed in <s>Unni</s>'s edition: 'one should supply the verb karoti.' (2) Brackets by <s>Sastri</s>; <s>Unni</s>: daṃseduṃ. (3) Note by <s>Sastri</s> (shortened in <s>Unni</s> 1998): 'argha is a root meaning the attainment of value; bahu is an adverb modifying the verb; the sense is that they attain great value, i.e., they receive no small praise. The purport is: he who, being himself a treasure-house of jewel-like verses rich in merits, does not despise the verses of others even if they are of small merit, but rather only praises them. yasmin is in the locative of the objective or proximate sense.' (4) Or does H omit pātrahastaḥ only? <s>Unni</s>'s note is ambiguous. (5) Or is it upādhaassa in K? The note in my edition is not clearly legible. (6) <s>Unni</s> does not make clear what the syllable gha is substituted for or where it is inserted. (7) Or suvihisasayyesu? (8) Brackets in both <s>Unni</s>'s and <s>Sastri</s>'s editions. (9) Probably for dhvaṃsaṃ. (10) No siglum in <s>Sastri</s>'s note. (11) <s>Unni</s> records the very same gṛhṇātu as a variant. (12) According to <s>Unni</s>. <s>Sastri</s> does not record any variant. (13) (Mis)printed: śvaṇṇena. (14) <s>Unni</s> prints (part of) the commentary in G: 'grāmasūkara means a dog; tasya galam means its throat; gaganam utpatitena mayā śvagaṇena saha airāvataṃ pratibhañjya gṛhītaḥ sasutas timiṅgila — this is the madman's raving.' (15) G comments: 'pūjayāmi; the remainder is: asya nayiṣye kapālam (I shall take his skull).' (16) <s>Unni</s> prints: bhagavān. (17) <s>Unni</s> prints: pūrvai. (18) No siglum added in <s>Unni</s>'s note.
